evidence.claim: Section 158 says the King appoints the Prime Minister on House approval, the Council of Ministers acts by collective responsibility, and the Prime Minister cannot hold office for more than eight years in total.
evidence.title: Constitution of the Kingdom of Thailand B.E. 2560 (2017)
evidence.publisher: Office of the Council of State via CYRILLA
evidence.excerpt: Section 158 says the King appoints the Prime Minister on House approval, the Council of Ministers acts by collective responsibility, and the Prime Minister cannot hold office for more than eight years in total.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text from an official legal translation repository.
evidence.period_fit: Sets the constitutional authority and hard constraint in force during 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines the institutional limits of Prayut's office rather than a personal nuclear mandate.
contrary_evidence: This is general executive authority, not nuclear-specific authority.

evidence.claim: Thailand reiterated support for a peaceful settlement through dialogue in line with the UN Charter and international law, and endorsed the Ukraine resolution adopted at the UN special session.
evidence.title: Weekly press briefing by MFA spokesperson on Thursday, 3 March 2022 at 11:30 hours
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand
evidence.excerpt: Thailand reiterated support for a peaceful settlement through dialogue in line with the UN Charter and international law, and endorsed the Ukraine resolution adopted at the UN special session.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official MFA briefing summarizing the government's immediate Ukraine response.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 response to the Ukraine invasion.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet/foreign-ministry level under Prayut, not a personal nuclear or battlefield decision.
contrary_evidence: The source reflects diplomatic posture rather than a discrete ruler-ordered military action.

evidence.claim: Thailand said it abstained because it wanted a transparent, impartial, and inclusive multilateral process that took verified facts and foreseeable consequences into account.
evidence.title: Explanation of Vote after the vote at the resumed 11th Emergency Special Session of the United Nations General Assembly 7 April 2022
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand
evidence.excerpt: Thailand said it abstained because it wanted a transparent, impartial, and inclusive multilateral process that took verified facts and foreseeable consequences into account.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary explanation of vote from Thailand's MFA.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to a major Ukraine-related UN vote.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State foreign-policy position under Prayut's government, not a personal command decision.
contrary_evidence: Abstention can be read as caution or as insufficient condemnation of Russia, depending on the frame.

evidence.claim: Thailand urged independent investigation, civilian protection, and compliance with international humanitarian law in Ukraine, while continuing to call for dialogue and accountability.
evidence.title: Explanation of Vote after the vote at the resumed 11th Emergency Special Session of the United Nations General Assembly 7 April 2022
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand
evidence.excerpt: Thailand urged independent investigation, civilian protection, and compliance with international humanitarian law in Ukraine, while continuing to call for dialogue and accountability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary explanation of vote with explicit civilian-protection language.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to the Ukraine war response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Foreign-policy and humanitarian stance of the Prayut government, not a personal battlefield act.
contrary_evidence: The vote was an abstention, so the source is mixed rather than purely favorable.

evidence.claim: Thailand said it was providing humanitarian assistance to Myanmar and coordinating with Cambodia and other actors to promote a peaceful political settlement.
evidence.title: Deputy Prime Minister/Minister of Foreign Affairs of Thailand chaired the 2nd Multi-Stakeholder Meeting on the Provision of Humanitarian Assistance for the People of Myanmar
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand
evidence.excerpt: Thailand said it was providing humanitarian assistance to Myanmar and coordinating with Cambodia and other actors to promote a peaceful political settlement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government record of a 2022 diplomacy and aid meeting.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and directly relevant to the Myanmar crisis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level action under Prayut's government; the meeting was chaired by the foreign minister, not Prayut personally.
contrary_evidence: Humanitarian coordination does not prove influence over the Myanmar military or the conflict itself.

evidence.claim: Thailand said it had worked with partners to provide humanitarian assistance to the Myanmar people and called for de-escalation, an end to violence, and meaningful talks to restore peace and stability.
evidence.title: Statement by H.E. Mr. Don Pramudwinai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Thailand at the General Debate of the 77th Session of the United Nations General Assembly
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand
evidence.excerpt: Thailand said it had worked with partners to provide humanitarian assistance to the Myanmar people and called for de-escalation, an end to violence, and meaningful talks to restore peace and stability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNGA statement from Thailand's foreign minister.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to both Myanmar and wider international peace issues.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government of Thailand position under Prayut; not a personal military command act by the prime minister.
contrary_evidence: The statement is ministerial and diplomatic, not direct evidence of Prayut's personal intervention.

evidence.claim: Thailand suggested Southeast Asian summit venues as possible off-ramps for the Ukraine crisis and urged the UN to help safeguard peace and stability.
evidence.title: Statement by H.E. Mr. Don Pramudwinai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Thailand at the General Debate of the 77th Session of the United Nations General Assembly
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand
evidence.excerpt: Thailand suggested Southeast Asian summit venues as possible off-ramps for the Ukraine crisis and urged the UN to help safeguard peace and stability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNGA statement from Thailand's foreign minister.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and directly relevant to crisis diplomacy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State diplomacy under Prayut's government, not a direct personal intervention by the PM.
contrary_evidence: This is an off-ramp proposal, not proof that Thailand could actually mediate the war.

evidence.claim: The UN envoy said Prayut had an important role in preventing further deterioration of the Myanmar crisis, and Prayut said Myanmar should be addressed gradually with understanding and trust.
evidence.title: U.N. envoy seeks Thai help to halt deterioration of Myanmar crisis
evidence.excerpt: The UN envoy said Prayut had an important role in preventing further deterioration of the Myanmar crisis, and Prayut said Myanmar should be addressed gradually with understanding and trust.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-reported contemporaneous coverage with direct quotes, republished by Euronews.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and directly tied to Thailand's Myanmar-border diplomacy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributes remarks to Prayut and to a UN envoy speaking to him.
contrary_evidence: The source does not show policy success, only engagement and an expressed preference for gradualism.

evidence.claim: Thailand's government said it was taking care of Myanmar refugees and carrying out its duties according to international human rights standards, while UNHCR said it lacked access to the Thai-hosted sites.
evidence.title: Fleeing violence in Myanmar, thousands camp along Thai border river
evidence.excerpt: Thailand's government said it was taking care of Myanmar refugees and carrying out its duties according to international human rights standards, while UNHCR said it lacked access to the Thai-hosted sites.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters field reporting with a quoted Thai government response and UNHCR follow-up.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to the Myanmar-border humanitarian setting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government response under Prayut; the refugee posture is state-level rather than a personal military order.
contrary_evidence: UNHCR access limits and reported camp problems weaken any simple favorable reading.

evidence.claim: Thailand said it abstained on the Ukraine territorial-integrity resolution because the situation was too volatile and charged, warned that escalation could raise the risk of nuclear weapons use, and urged serious negotiation.
evidence.title: Weekly press briefing by MFA on Wednesday, 19 October 2022
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand
evidence.excerpt: Thailand said it abstained on the Ukraine territorial-integrity resolution because the situation was too volatile and charged, warned that escalation could raise the risk of nuclear weapons use, and urged serious negotiation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary Thai MFA briefing documenting the government's explanation of its UN abstention.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and directly related to the Ukraine war's diplomatic handling.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level position under Prayut's government, not a personal battlefield decision.
contrary_evidence: The abstention is mixed evidence because it avoided full condemnation while still affirming opposition to force.

evidence.claim: Thailand hosted an informal consultation on Myanmar that produced a first face-to-face discussion with Myanmar's foreign minister in more than a year, focusing on humanitarian assistance and a political solution.
evidence.title: Weekly press briefing by MFA on Friday, 23 December 2022
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand
evidence.excerpt: Thailand hosted an informal consultation on Myanmar that produced a first face-to-face discussion with Myanmar's foreign minister in more than a year, focusing on humanitarian assistance and a political solution.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary year-end MFA briefing on Thailand's Myanmar diplomacy.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and directly relevant to conflict de-escalation efforts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State diplomacy under Prayut's government, not a personal military order.
contrary_evidence: The source describes consultation and aspiration, not a verified end to the Myanmar conflict.

unresolved_gaps: No Prayut-specific 2022 nuclear or other existential-risk choice is evidenced; the package is mostly inherited treaty and safeguards context.
No direct cabinet-minute or NSC record ties Prayut personally to each 2022 Ukraine or Myanmar diplomatic position.
Direct command-chain evidence for specific police operations, protest policing, and protest-prosecution decisions is limited.
Direct documentary proof of Prayut's personal authorization of spyware or surveillance is absent.
Ruler-level evidence on appointments quality and 2022 rule-setting for competition, property rights, and investment remains thin.
Outcome evidence is stronger than direct ruler attribution across health, education, and social protection.
No direct 2022 evidence of hidden assets, family profit, or proven deception beyond disclosure opacity and allegations.
There is no single consolidated FY2022 execution audit tying the program, implementation, and outcomes back to Prayut's full cabinet-level agenda.
